text:
emi: Proposal — surface an "effective SLO" in Console and the internal API that shows the threshold after routing rules, tenant quotas, and noisy-suppression are applied. Need early API shape feedback.

jonah: Sounds useful. Do you mean the value we actually use to trigger alerts (post-routing) vs the configured SLO?

emi: Exactly. Configured SLO is the source of truth, but teams keep asking why alerts fire even though their SLO looks fine in the editor. The gap is usually routing fallback or per-tenant throttles.

priya: Could be helpful for debugging. Two quick asks: 1) make it queryable by timeframe and evaluation window, 2) include which rule caused the adjustment (eg. "quota_cap", "region_fallback", "noise_mute").

andre: Agreed. Also add the last-evaluation-reason and the id of the policy that adjusted it. Otherwise support has to stitch traces.

emi: Proposed minimal API: GET /v1/console/effective_slo?route=<id>&tenant=<id>&window=5m -> returns the effective threshold and an ordered list of modifiers. Example response we were thinking: 

```
{
  "route_id": "rt-123",
  "tenant_id": "t-999",
  "configured_slo": 0.995,
  "effective_slo": 0.990,
  "modifiers": [
    {"type": "quota_cap", "value": 0.992, "policy_id": "q-12"},
    {"type": "region_fallback", "value": 0.990, "policy_id": "r-3"}
  ],
  "evaluated_at": "2026-03-20T14:12:00Z"
}
```

jonah: That shape seems fine. A couple of notes: return values should be numbers (not strings), but we'll handle that in SDK mapping. Also include a short text field like `reason_summary` for Console tooltips.

priya: How will this impact telemetry volume? If Console calls this for many routes/tenants we could multiply queries. We should add caching + an inexpensive metrics endpoint like /v1/console/effective_slo/batch.

sre-bot: Suggestion: emit a telemetry event `slo.effective_eval` whenever the effective_slo deviates > 0.001 from configured for any route. Fields: route_id, tenant_id, configured_slo, effective_slo, modifiers_count.

andre: Love the event. That lets us build a dashboard for drift and noisy tenants. Also, add `notify.fanout_count` and `last_notify_policy` to the event so we can correlate alert spam.

emi: For Console UX: show the configured SLO (editable), then a collapsed row "effective SLO (what will fire)" with a hover that lists modifiers and the last-change time. Also a "why did this change?" link that opens the trace in Ops.

jonah: Rollout plan idea: behind a feature flag for 2 weeks, only for internal+beta tenants. Add a sticky notice in the editor: "values shown may differ from configured SLO due to routing/quotas."

priya: Implementation notes: runtime already computes these modifiers during evaluation—we can surface the same structure. We should standardize modifier types in enum: [quota_cap, region_fallback, noisy_suppression, manual_override]. Don't invent more ad-hoc strings.

andre: API auth: only console service tokens + support roles can call the endpoint. Batch endpoint accepts up to 50 queries per call. Throttle at 10rps per console instance.

emi: Question for eng-platform: do we want to add the effective threshold into alert payloads sent to downstream notifiers? That would help recipients avoid double-alerting, but it's a behavior change.

jonah: I'd prefer to include it in metadata for a follow-up release (non-blocking). First release: read-only Console/API visibility.

priya: Can we add a small unit test matrix for the modifier precedence? e.g., quota_cap > noisy_suppression > region_fallback > manual_override (manual last). We'll put that in the eval tests.

andre: I'll draft the API PR. emi can you add the Console mockups and telemetry event spec? I'll wire auth and rate limits.

emi: On it. I'll post mocks and the telemetry spec (including metric names: `slo.effective_delta`, `notify.fanout_count`) in #eng-platform later today. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy note: flag `console_effective_slo_v1` created. Will be false by default.

emi: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow if anyone has objections.
